The Newest Mobi XL Tiny House Adds an Extra Room to a Luxurious Layout
46 photos
Photo: Mobi House
How to make an XL tiny house even better – that is something where Mobi House excels. This highly reputable European builder with one of the most prolific portfolios on the market is an expert in modern Scandinavian-style tiny homes, from the ultra-compact ones to luxurious XL designs. Its latest model, the Mobi Kolos Island, takes things to a new level.
When you say XL tiny house, you immediately think of a supremely spacious layout that doesn’t sacrifice any of the common living spaces of a conventional house. With Mobi Kolos Island, the newest addition to its Mobile Line series, Mobi House enhances flexibility by adding an extra room that can become many things, depending on each owner’s preferences and needs.
Mobile Line is the Polish builder’s premium home series, comprised of 10-meter-long (32.8 feet) models with full-size bedrooms, kitchens, lounges, and bathrooms. Ideal for families but just as great for couples and individual owners who simply want the comfort of uncompromising spaciousness, the XL tiny homes in this series are all about luxury.
Photo: Mobi House After the success of Mobi Kolos Mountains, Mobi Kolos Sea, and Mobi Kolos Desert, the Polish builder is truly breaking the norm with a new model that is more impressive than anything before it. Mobi Kolos Island is really a mini mansion on wheels, extremely versatile , and beautifully furnished in the best Scandinavian style.
A proven two-bedroom layout with a ground-floor bedroom and a loft is made even more versatile by adding an extra room defined as a multi-purpose space. Smaller than the ground-floor two-person bedroom, this compact room can be turned into a second ground-floor bedroom for one, a kids’ room with bunk beds, a lovely, private home office, or even a spacious walk-in wardrobe (just the idea of a tiny house with a separate walk-in wardrobe is pure luxury).
A generous 3-meter (9.8 feet) width, together with the XL length, leads to a spacious layout offering more than 26 square meters (280 square feet) of floor space. As a result, future owners will be able to enjoy a perfect kitchen, a lounge/dining area that’s big enough for the entire family, a stylish bathroom, and multiple bedrooms that can comfortably accommodate up to six people.
Photo: Mobi House The wagon-like configuration includes a wide corridor from one end of the house to another, while all the living and service areas spill effortlessly from one another. This type of design is highly space-efficient and also modern, with the corridor adding just the right level of separation, as well as seamless access from one end of the home to the other. Large windows throughout keep the entire home filled with natural light, making it seem even bigger.
A modern configuration like this strikes the perfect balance between privacy and openness. In a tiny house, personal space can sometimes be challenging, just as much as bringing people together around the dining table. This new XL tiny house takes care of both issues. With the main bedroom and the extra multi-purpose room, it adds two enclosed spaces for full privacy, while the lounge is big enough to welcome all six people.
The lounge itself is a flexible space. Owners can choose to use it as a classic living room. In that case, it would be furnished with a typical Mobi custom sofa bench, an L-shaped design with built-in storage and comfy cushioning. A large TV mounted on the wall and a classic coffee table complete the setup. If they choose to turn this into a dining room, there’s enough space for an ingenious foldable oak table, with bench seats on one side, and regular chairs on the other side.
Photo: Mobi House This gorgeous dining room version, inspired by diner booths, is one of the most spacious and comfortable you’ll ever see in a tiny house. It doesn’t just make room for the whole family, but it offers the best view on both sides – those seated on the bench are facing the main entry, which is entirely glazed, while those seated on the chairs are facing the two large, horizontal windows in the lounge, separate by a custom shelf for storage and decorative display.
Nestled between the kitchen and the bedroom exterior wall, this versatile lounge/dining room feels a lot cozier, too. Plus, that exterior wall (cleverly turned into a feature wall for a style boost) acts as the perfect canvas for additional décor, which makes this relaxation nook even more elegant.
The kitchen is also U-shaped, with an L-shaped countertop on one side, and a full cabinetry wall on the other side. This is the kind of tiny house kitchen where nobody will miss the storage capacity of a conventional kitchen. Lower cupboards, floating shelves, and a full cabinetry wall offer monster storage that will keep everything perfectly organized.
Photo: Mobi House High-quality appliances are also impeccably incorporated, including a dishwasher and a washer/dryer that wouldn’t fit in the bathroom. The furniture is custom-made, so owners can choose between laminated plywood, oak, or composite, depending on their budget and style preferences. Expensive finishes can take this XL tiny house to a truly luxurious level, comparable to a mini-mansion.
The main bedroom also features a lot of built-in cabinets and generous closet space beyond what you could typically expect in a tiny house. It’s true that the bulkiness of the cabinetry makes this room seem less spacious and a bit cramped, but ample storage is what most people want when considering long-term accommodation in a tiny house. In other words, a tiny house bedroom with lots of free floor space and large windows looks great, but isn’t very practical long-term.
The loft bedroom is accessed via a regular ladder, from the spare room area. This is a small loft, with a two-person bed mattress, a tiny window, and not much else. It can accommodate two guests, but the ladder access and compact floor space makes it less appealing for long-term accommodation. However, the Mobi Kolos Island is also available in a loft-free version, for those who prefer a single-level layout.
Photo: Mobi House Located at one end of the house, the bathroom is compact, but elegantly equipped and styled. A floating toilet design with a concealed cistern saves floor space and also looks more modern, while a full-size shower cabin takes up one end of the bathroom. Small but thoughtful details like the towel rack, the elegant vanity, and the large mirror turn this into a stylish bathroom.
Heating comes from a wide range of options, from split air conditioning to underfloor heating, infrared panels, or convection heaters. A complex layer of thermal insulation works to keep this XL tiny house comfortable in any season and safe from humidity. A high-quality timber frame provides the backbone for this XL abode, with exterior cladding made of Scandinavian spruce or thermally-treated pine (combined with metal panels).
Mobi Kolos Island comes on a dedicated low-speed trailer by MH Trailers, the tiny house trailer company created by Mobi House. With a weight of more than 3.5 tons, this XL tiny house is not intended as a road companion, like the smaller tiny homes, but the trailer makes it easy to transport to its final location.
Photo: Mobi House Ideal for families and for anyone who wants downsizing without compromise, this new XL tiny house brings together timeless Scandinavian elegance and an ultra-flexible layout for comfort that truly feels like home.
